cells.tense: The direction you chose is still being walked, and the hand that chose it is on the pen at this table now.
cells.act: balance the competing demands and keep tending
cells.ask: Sort this week's demands into two groups: what the chosen direction needs, and what is only loud. Tend the first group. The second can stay where you can see it, untouched.
cells.core:
You said 'this, not that' and kept walking it. There is a way picking shows when it's working: the effort still goes where pointed, nobody has to check on you, and the care isn't costing you anything you'd notice. What you built from your own reserves keeps getting looked after on the days you're not watching. You hold the pen here, and the line stays straight.

The next thing this balance can feed is cultivating what you've chosen with steady care, and it's one act: balance the competing demands and keep tending. Some weeks that takes minutes, some weeks all seven days, and it still isn't clutching. If a demand stands over there untended all week, that's a message you can read at the end of it, once. What you look after decides the direction without a scene.
cells.sheetLine: The direction holds because you keep tending it.

cells.tense: The direction is being checked and re-checked before it has arrived, as if the next move could be rehearsed into safety.
cells.act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve
cells.ask: Look at the list you're carrying for the direction you chose. Strike one thing off it that does not serve. Do it now. Keep the struck list where you'll see it once tomorrow.
cells.core:
You're steering, and the steering has become a practice of checking — whether the last move landed, whether the next one will. The direction is real; the review of it runs faster than the road. What was chosen is held so tightly that holding takes the hours walking needed.

The next thing this balance can feed is sorting what matters from what doesn't, and it's one act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve. One line, gone, and the direction is still yours. The effort you were spending on review goes back into walking. If you strike the wrong thing, you'll know by the week's close without having looked.

The cost of this balance is that the list grows back. Pruning is the practice, not the cure.

cells.tense: The direction was chosen, and the walking stopped at a door you have already gone through.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Take what the chosen direction actually needs from you this week — your share of it, all of it — and carry that. Nothing extra. If your share is small, carry the small share fully, and stop there.
cells.core:
You chose a direction once, and it has gone quiet. The effort that used to go toward it now goes toward not being asked about it. You're still at the table, but the pen isn't being picked up. The will that said 'this, not that' is present and isn't pointed at anything.

The next thing this balance can feed is persisting on what you have, and it's one act: carry your own share, all of it. Not more, to prove something, and not less, to stay unasked. Your share, wholly, is enough for now. Strength comes back through material — through doing the next necessary thing with your own hands and stopping when it's done.

What you carry this week doesn't need an audience. The direction is still yours.

cells.tense: The direction was chosen and followed, and the choosing of it is filed under something else — luck, circumstance, what the moment required.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Pick one resource the chosen direction uses — time, money, attention. Give it one deliberate act of care. Then, looking back later, notice who chose to give it.
cells.core:
You're steering — saying 'this, not that' and meaning it — and the steering gets attributed to the situation. The direction you chose is being walked; the author of the walk is filed under what the moment called for. The pen is moving and you'd say it moves by itself.

The next thing this balance can feed is looking after what you've chosen with steady care, and it's one act: tend the resource with responsible care. Choose one thing the direction uses, tend it on purpose, and put your name on the moment you chose it. Not a plan, not a telling — just the doing with the author present. The resource already knows whose it is. This is only so you know it too.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: 'what was quietly given up is now seen and valued by the group' — the record says external acknowledgment completes this capacity, but I can't put the acknowledgment, or the group's seeing, into the person's present. The reader could reasonably object: 'I never gave anything up where anyone noticed.' The asks survive that: Stewardship and Steadfastness are the person's own acts, done alone, and Honing strikes from the person's own list, so no one else has to be present or fair for the act to work. The line that serves the writer more than the person is anything that tells them how their effort is received; the cells keep to what the person does and what follows, never who acknowledges it.
